study.title: One elite vaulter's insertional Achilles case: isometrics mentioned, never dosed or tested

full_text.why: Whole collection read from the free PMC full text (PMC8700006); fetch tool paraphrased, so wording is mine. Each abstract is all there is.

key_findings: Collection doesn't answer the isometrics question: no abstract tests isometrics for mid-portion Achilles pain
Closest: single case, elite pole vaulter, insertional (not mid-portion) Achilles tendinopathy
Isometrics plus heel lift used for 2 weeks only; dose not reported
VISA-A up 20 points over 4 months with fenestration plus progressive loading
One patient, three treatments at once: can't credit isometrics with anything
summary: 22 conference abstracts from the first IJSPT research forum at OSET, Las Vegas, December 2021
Card covers abstract 5: Dewald M, tendon fenestration in a professional pole vaulter with insertional Achilles tendinopathy
Fenestration dry needling twice, isometrics and heel lift for 2 weeks, then weekly-progressed loading for 4 months
Pain-free running and jumping by 4 months; tendon thinner and stiffer
Editors say the abstracts can't be judged for rigour and results are preliminary
study.bottom_line: Nothing here changes how you use isometrics for early mid-portion Achilles pain. The one relevant case is insertional, elite, uncontrolled and undosed. Keep following the Atlas loading playbook.

design: No registration; none expected for a case report
methods.setting: Not reported; author is at the University of South Dakota, USA
participants: 2-year left insertional Achilles tendinopathy limiting competition
intervention: Tendon fenestration dry needling, sessions 1–2: 10 parallel passes toward the insertion from ~2 cm proximal
Isometrics plus heel lift for the first 2 weeks; dose not reported
Then loading progressed weekly for 4 months: Silbernagel protocol, then Baxter loading index
Plus lower-limb strengthening and plyometrics; sets, reps, frequency not reported
methods.primary_outcome: VISA-A; also ultrasound thickness and MyotonPro stiffness

results.detail: Final score not given. Abstract states MCID 6.5 points without citing a source. Single case, so no effect estimate or CI.
Ultrasound. Baseline showed no break in fibrillar structure. Assessor and blinding not reported.

results.meaning: Surface myotonometry, not tendon mechanics proper
results.detail: MyotonPro, mean of 3 readings. Abstract reports a 120 N/m rise; the figures give 119. Stiffness vs VISA-A r=0.75 and vs thickness r=−0.89; number of paired measures not stated.
Competition return implied by the authors but no competition data given.

pico.p: One 28-year-old elite female pole vaulter with 2-year insertional Achilles tendinopathy
pico.i: Tendon fenestration dry needling, 2 weeks of isometrics and heel lift, then progressive loading
pico.o: VISA-A, ultrasound thickness, myotonometric stiffness, return to running and jumping at 4 months

limits: Single uncontrolled case; three treatments given together
Isometric dose, position and load not reported
Conference abstract only; no full peer-reviewed report
how_to_apply: Don't change your early isometric dosing on the strength of this abstract.
Keep using isometrics as a short, symptom-guided entry to loading, then progress.
Don't add fenestration dry needling for mid-portion pain based on one insertional case.
Track VISA-A at baseline and monthly.
Treat a VISA-A rise of 6.5 points or more as worth noting.
applies_to: Chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy in jumping athletes
Context only: isometrics as a brief entry phase before loading
not_for: Deciding isometric dose for mid-portion Achilles pain

domains.domain: History clearly described as a timeline

domains.reason: Change scores given, but final VISA-A and competition outcome not reported.

grade.reason: Single uncontrolled case, co-interventions, unblinded outcomes, abstract only.
Insertional not mid-portion; elite athlete; isometrics never isolated or dosed.
n=1; no CI possible; far below any optimal information size.
Successful cases are the ones written up as conference abstracts.

clinical_significance: VISA-A +20 exceeds the abstract's stated 6.5-point MCID
The abstract gives no source for that MCID
Change in one person can't show the effect of any component
Nothing on isometrics' own effect on pain or function
comparator_fairness: Can't separate needling, isometrics, heel lift, loading or time
alternative_explanations: Progressive loading alone could explain the change
Natural history and regression to the mean after a bad spell
Expectation effects from a novel needling procedure
Training modification during rehab not reported
spin: Concludes fenestration is promising from one case with co-interventions
Correlations from one person read as mechanism
fit_with_evidence: Loading as core treatment fits the Atlas Achilles playbook and current guidelines
Clifford 2020 review of RCTs: isometrics no better than isotonic loading for pain; this case adds nothing
Fenestration for Achilles lacks controlled trial support
external_validity: ✓ Loading progression familiar to Australian clinicians
would_change_my_mind: A controlled trial isolating early isometrics in mid-portion Achilles pain
A full case series with isometric dose and pain response per session
strengths: Objective tendon measures at baseline and 4 months
appraisal.funding_conflicts: None stated for the abstract. The forum was sponsored by ATI Physical Therapy and Hyperice; no link to this case stated.

disagreements.why: Only the author's affiliation is given.
Tests named; assessor, blinding, reliability not reported.
disagreements.resolved: Agreed: some concerns. Overall RoB stays high.

disagreements.why: Abstract never describes the care setting.

disagreements.second: split step; move logs; name a source

verification.external_searched: site:pedro.org.au searches for the collection and the pole-vaulter case: none (abstracts not indexed). Web search for reviews citing the case: none.

study.patient_explanation: This was one athlete with pain where the tendon joins the heel. She got better over four months with needling and a gradually harder exercise plan. It doesn't tell us much about holding exercises for pain higher up the tendon.
open_questions: Do early isometrics improve mid-portion Achilles pain more than isotonic loading?
What isometric dose, if any, gives useful short-term pain relief in early-stage patients?
Does fenestration add anything to loading in a controlled trial?
Was this case ever published in full?
study.evidence_note: Single conference-abstract case. Loading message matches the playbook; isometrics and needling claims untested here.
study.confidence_note: Whole collection read on PMC via paraphrasing fetches. Other Achilles abstracts (stiffness in runners; Sever's case) lack isometrics. No full paper found.
study.impact_line: Collection has nothing to guide isometrics for mid-portion Achilles pain; one insertional case used them briefly, undosed.

sources.citation: Page P, et al. The Inaugural IJSPT and OSET Research Symposium: 2021 Abstracts. Int J Sports Phys Ther 2021;16(6):1595-1607. In: Dewald M. Treatment of a professional pole vaulter with insertional Achilles tendinopathy using tendon fenestration.
